facts.statement: The skull of Talarurus measured approximately 30 centimeters in total length.

facts.statement: The most complete skull of Talarurus is specimen MPC-D 100/1354.

facts.statement: Each maxilla of Talarurus preserves 23 tooth sockets, though no teeth were found in the fossils.
facts.quote: Each maxilla preserves 23 alveoli, however, the teeth were not preserved.

facts.statement: Lower jaw remains are rare in Talarurus, but specimen MPC-D 100/1355 was found with a fragmented right dentary.
facts.quote: Usually, the lower jaw remains of Talarurus do not preserve, however, MPC-D 100/1355 was found in association with a right dentary, very fragmented though.

facts.statement: Ribs from Talarurus specimens are strongly curved and thickened, measuring between 50 and 100 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: Based on the PIN 557 specimens, the ribs are strongly curved and thickened, having a length ranging between 50 and 100 cm.

facts.statement: The sacrum of Talarurus consists of four presacral vertebrae, four sacral vertebrae, and the first caudal vertebra, all fused together with attached ribs.
facts.quote: The sacrum consists of 4 presacrals, 4 sacrals, and the first caudal vertebra, these vertebrae are fused together, with some ribs attached.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests the tail of Talarurus consisted of approximately 25 to 30 caudal vertebrae.
facts.quote: Some isolated caudal vertebrae are present, they seem to indicate that the tail consisted of approximately 25 to 30 caudals.

facts.statement: Preserved osteoderms on Talarurus are sparse, including cervical halfrings and spine-shaped body osteoderms that measured up to 15 centimeters in height.
facts.quote: The preserved osteoderms are very sparse, consisting of some cervical halfrings and spine-shaped body osteoderms. The osteoderms are strongly robust, most spine-shaped osteoderms measured 15 cm in height.

facts.statement: Only the left hand of Talarurus is preserved, and it is virtually complete with five digits, though some claws and finger bones are missing.
facts.quote: Only the left manus is preserved, it is virtually complete preserving five digits, only lacking some unguals and phalanges.

facts.statement: The preserved left foot of Talarurus likely had three digits, correcting an earlier mistaken description of four digits caused by the initial skeleton mount.
facts.quote: The preserved left pes is unique; it was described as having four digits, this statement however, was proved to be a product of the initial skeleton mount and three digits is more accurate/likely, as seen in related ankylosaurines.

facts.statement: The shoulder girdle of Talarurus includes a scapulocoracoid measuring about 60 centimeters long, along with robust humerus, radius, and ulna belonging to the left arm.
facts.quote: The shoulder girdle is represented by a scapulocoracoid that measures about 60 cm long, humerus, radius and ulna, these elements are very robust compared to other postcrania and they pertain to the left arm.

facts.statement: The humerus of Talarurus is thickened and measures 33.5 centimeters in length, showing some resemblance to that of Ankylosaurus.
facts.quote: The humerus is very wide at the ends and thickened measuring 33.5 cm long; it shows some resemblance to that of Ankylosaurus.

facts.statement: The preserved femur of Talarurus is straight, strongly robust, and measures 47 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: The preserved femur is straight and strongly robust, the greater trochanter is fused with the lesser trochanter; it measures 47 cm long.

facts.statement: The tibia of Talarurus is shortened but very wide, with a total length of 29.8 centimeters.
facts.quote: The tibia however, is more shortened but greatly wide, it has a total length of 29.8 cm.

facts.statement: A preserved fibula from Talarurus measures 26.7 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: In addition, a fibula was also preserved, it has a length of 26.7 cm.

facts.statement: Maleev originally assigned Talarurus to the family Syrmosauridae in 1952, which is now known as Ankylosauridae.
facts.quote: Talarurus was assigned to the Syrmosauridae (now known as Ankylosauridae) by Maleev in its original description in 1952.

facts.statement: Recent phylogenetic analysis places Talarurus within the Ankylosaurinae, a derived subgroup of ankylosaurids.
facts.quote: Recent phylogenetic analysis provides evidence for an assignment of Talarurus to the Ankylosaurinae, a derived ankylosaurid group.

facts.statement: Arbour's 2014 analysis suggests Talarurus is more closely related to North American ankylosaurids than to Asian forms.
facts.quote: However, Arbour in 2014 recovered trees in which Talarurus was more closely related to North-American forms than to Asian ankylosaurids.

facts.statement: Studies of the endocranial region indicate that ankylosaurids like Talarurus had well-developed gaze stabilization and auditory senses, unlike nodosaurids.
facts.quote: They noted that ankylosaurids had well-developed gaze stabilization and auditive senses, differing from nodosaurids, by examining the endocranial region of the selected specimens.

facts.statement: The flocculus, a brain structure related to balance, was first reported in Talarurus and is common in ankylosaurids but absent or reduced in nodosaurids.
facts.quote: The presence of the flocculus was first reported in Talarurus by Maryańska and later in other related ankylosaurids, however, this lobe seems to be absent or reduced in nodosaurids.

facts.statement: Ankylosaurids like Talarurus possessed a large range of sound perception, particularly for low frequencies, based on their anatomy.
facts.quote: This anatomical feature indicates that ankylosaurids had a large range of sound perception, especially for low frequencies.

facts.statement: The wide, stocky rostrum of Talarurus suggests it was an efficient grazer feeding on low vegetation in flat terrain.
facts.quote: The wide rostrum of Talarurus probably worked with efficiency on low vegetation at flat terrain. Evidence seems to indicate that Talarurus had a grazer feeding-method.

facts.statement: It is unclear whether slight differences in caputegulae on skull roof PIN 3780/1 represent a taxonomic issue, according to Arbour and Currie.
facts.quote: As noted by Arbour and Currie, the skull roof of PIN 3780/1 appears to have slightly different caputegulae (head osteoderms or armour tiles), and that it was unclear if this represents a taxonomic issue.

facts.statement: Walter Preston Coombs suggested Talarurus was the same species as Euoplocephalus, but later studies did not support this claim.
facts.quote: Walter Preston Coombs suggested that it was the same dinosaur as Euoplocephalus although subsequent study did not support this assertion.

facts.statement: Talarurus lived during the Late Cretaceous period, approximately 96 to 89 million years ago.
facts.quote: The fossil remains of Talarurus have been found in the sediments of Bayan Shireh Formation, which are thought to date from the Cenomanian to Santonian stages of the Late Cretaceous period, about 96 million to 89 million years ago.

facts.statement: This dinosaur lived in what is now Asia during the Turonian stage of the mid-Cretaceous.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 96 a 89 millones de años, durante el Turoniense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: Research suggests Talarurus was a grazer herbivore, while its contemporary Tsagantegia was a browser herbivore.
facts.quote: According to Park et al. 2019, Talarurus filled the niche of a grazer herbivore, whereas Tsagantegia, another ankylosaurid from the formation, filled the niche of a browser herbivore.

facts.statement: Talarurus possessed a broad, rectangular snout adapted for grazing low vegetation.
facts.quote: For instance, Talarurus had a broad and rectangular snout (or beak), useful for low vegetation, while the one in Tsagantegia is more elongated and shovel-shaped, useful for high vegetation.

facts.statement: Talarurus was a medium-sized, heavy quadruped that grew up to 5 meters long and weighed between 454 and 907 kilograms.
facts.quote: Era un herbívoro cuadrúpedo de tamaño mediano, corpulento, que vivía en el suelo , que podía crecer hasta 5 metros de largo y pesaba alrededor de 454 a 907 kilogramos, entre media y una tonelada.

facts.statement: Like other ankylosaurids, Talarurus had heavy armor and a club on its tail, which limited its speed.
facts.quote: Al igual que otros anquilosáuridos, tenía una armadura pesada y un garrote en la cola, lo que limitaba su velocidad.

facts.statement: The osteoderms featured furrowed ornamentation, creating a formidable armor with each plate adorned with additional pleated spines.
facts.quote: Otra supuesta característica, los osteodermos tenían una ornamentación surcada, formando una armadura especialmente formidable, con cada placa adornada con espinas plisadas adicionales.

facts.statement: A unique autapomorphy identified in the frontals is a V-shaped elevated region on the middle roof of the skull.
facts.quote: Estableció una autapomorfía única, en los frontales, en el techo medio del cráneo, está presente una región elevada en forma de V.

facts.statement: Talarurus is distinguished from all known ankylosaurids except Nodocephalosaurus by possessing conical caputegulas with circular bases on the frontals and nasals.
facts.quote: Talarurus se diferenciaba de todos los anquilosáuridos conocidos con la excepción del norteamericano Nodocephalosaurus en la posesión de caputegulas, osteodermos o placas de armadura faciales, en los frontales y nasales, que tienen forma de cono con base circular.

facts.statement: The first remains of Talarurus were discovered in 1948 and described by Russian paleontologist Evgeny Maleev.
facts.quote: Los primeros restos de Talarurus fueron descubiertos en 1948 y posteriormente descritos por el paleontólogo ruso Evgeny Maleev, llamando a la especie tipo T. plicatospineus.

facts.statement: Known from multiple but scarce specimens, Talarurus is one of the most famous ankylosaurids alongside Pinacosaurus.
facts.quote: Se conoce a partir de múltiples pero escasos especímenes, lo que lo convierte en uno de los anquilosáuridos más conocidos, junto con Pinacosaurus.

facts.statement: Five skulls have been discovered and assigned to the genus, though the first two were very fragmentary.
facts.quote: Se han descubierto y asignado al género cinco cráneos, aunque los dos primeros estaban muy fragmentados.

facts.statement: Although initially described with four toes, evidence suggests Talarurus likely had three toes, consistent with other known ankylosaurids.
facts.quote: Inicialmente, Maleev describió a Talarurus con cuatro dedos en el pie. Sin embargo, el pie no se encontró en articulación. El pie montado es un compuesto, y tres es el número más probable, ya que todos los demás anquilosáuridos conocidos muestran tres dedos.

facts.statement: Early diagnoses by Maleev (1956) and Tumanova (1987) were of limited utility because they listed many shared traits common to other ankylosaurids.
facts.quote: Los diagnósticos proporcionados por Maleev 1956 y Tumanova 1987 fueron de utilidad limitada ya que enumeraban en gran medida rasgos compartidos con muchos otros anquilosáuridos.

facts.statement: The species Talarurus plicatospineus was named by Maleev in 1952.
facts.quote: genus: Talarurus species: T. plicatospineus species_authority: Maleev, 1952

facts.statement: Talarurus is classified within the family Ankylosauridae and the subfamily Ankylosaurinae.
facts.quote: familia: Ankylosauridae subfamilia: Ankylosaurinae

facts.statement: Nodocephalosaurus, a North American ankylosaurid with similar facial osteoderms, appears to be the closest relative of Talarurus.
facts.quote: Parece que el pariente más cercano de Talarurus era Nodocephalosaurus , un anquilosáurido con osteodermos faciales similares de América del Norte.

facts.statement: Most skeletal mounts of Talarurus are outdated due to numerous anatomical errors, such as ribs pointing downward instead of outward as seen in most ankylosaurids.
facts.quote: La mayoría de las monturas esqueléticas de Talarurus están desactualizadas por numerosos problemas, como que las costillas apuntan hacia abajo en lugar de hacia los lados, como en la mayoría de los anquilosáuridos.

facts.statement: Previous mounts depicted Talarurus with a barrel-shaped chest and widely separated forelimbs, resembling a hippopotamus rather than the low, wide body typical of ankylosaurids.
facts.quote: El montaje tiene la particularidad adicional de que muestra a Talarurus como construido como un hipopótamo, con un tórax en forma de barril, no con el tipo de cuerpo bajo y ancho característico de los anquilosáuridos, y las extremidades anteriores están fuertemente separadas.

facts.statement: The most complete skull specimen is MPC-D 100/1354.
facts.quote: El cráneo más completo es el MPC-D 100/1354.

facts.statement: Each jaw preserves 23 tooth sockets, though the teeth themselves are not preserved.
facts.quote: Cada maxilar conserva 23 alvéolos, sin embargo, los dientes no se conservaron.

facts.statement: Most caputegulae on the top of the head are hexagonal, though some in the holotype PIN 557-91 are triangular.
facts.quote: La mayoría de las caputegulas presentes en la parte superior de la cabeza son de forma hexagonal, en el holotipo PIN 557-91 algunas son triangulares.

facts.statement: According to specimens PIN 557, the ribs are strongly curved and thickened, with a length ranging between 50 and 100 cm.
facts.quote: Según los especímenes PIN 557, las nervaduras están fuertemente curvadas y engrosadas, con una longitud que oscila entre 50 y 100 cm.

facts.statement: The sacrum consists of 4 presacral, 4 sacral, and the first caudal vertebrae.
facts.quote: el sacro consta de 4 presacras, 4 sacros y la primera vértebra caudal

facts.statement: The tail consisted of approximately 25 to 30 caudal vertebrae.
facts.quote: la cola constaba de aproximadamente 25 a 30 caudales.

facts.statement: The osteoderms are strongly robust, with most column-shaped osteoderms measuring 15 cm in height.
facts.quote: Los osteodermos son fuertemente robustos, la mayoría de los osteodermos en forma de columna miden 15 cm de altura.

facts.statement: The left scapulocoracoid is very robust with a well-developed insertion for the humerus and glenoid cavity, although the scapular blade is somewhat shorter in length.
facts.quote: El escapulocoracoides izquierdo es muy robusto con una inserción bien desarrollada para el húmero, cavidad glenoide, aunque la hoja escapular es algo más corta en longitud.

facts.statement: The humerus is very wide at the ends and thickened, measuring 33.5 cm (335 mm) in length.
facts.quote: El húmero es muy ancho en los extremos y engrosado mide 33,5 cm (335 mm) de largo

facts.statement: The preserved femur is straight and strongly robust, with the greater trochanter fused to the lesser trochanter and measuring 47 cm in length.
facts.quote: El fémur preservado es recto y fuertemente robusto, el trocánter mayor está fusionado con el trocánter menor y mide 47 cm de largo.

facts.statement: The tibia is shorter but very wide, with a total length of 29.8 cm.
facts.quote: La tibia, sin embargo, es más corta pero muy ancha, tiene una longitud total de 29,8 cm.

facts.statement: Additionally, a fibula was preserved with a length of 26.7 cm.
facts.quote: Además, también se conservó un peroné tiene una longitud de 26,7 cm.

facts.statement: The preserved left foot was initially described as having four digits, but this was proven to be an artifact of the initial skeleton mount, with three digits being more probable.
facts.quote: El pie izquierdo conservado es muy singular, se describió que tenía cuatro dígitos, sin embargo, se demostró que esta afirmación era un producto del montaje del esqueleto inicial y tres dígitos es más probable

facts.statement: Talarurus was assigned to Syrmosauridae, now known as Ankylosauridae, by Maleev in his original description in 1952.
facts.quote: Talarurus fue asignado a Syrmosauridae, ahora conocido como Ankylosauridae, por Maleev en su descripción original en 1952.

facts.statement: Walter Preston Coombs suggested it was the same dinosaur as Euoplocephalus, though later studies did not support this claim.
facts.quote: Walter Preston Coombs sugirió que era el mismo dinosaurio que Euoplocephalus, aunque estudios posteriores no respaldaron esta afirmación.

facts.statement: Recent phylogenetic analysis provides evidence for assigning Talarurus to Ankylosaurinae, a derived group of ankylosaurids.
facts.quote: El análisis filogenético reciente proporciona evidencia de una asignación de Talarurus a los Ankylosaurinae, un grupo derivado de anquilosáuridos.

facts.statement: Vickaryous et al. (2004) noted the presence of two distinct ankylosaurid clades during the Late Cretaceous, one composed of North American taxa and the other restricted to Asian taxa.

facts.statement: However, Arbour (2014) recovered trees in which Talarurus was more closely related to North American forms than to Asian ankylosaurids.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, Arbor en 2014 recuperó árboles en los que Talarurus estaba más estrechamente relacionado con las formas norteamericanas que con los anquilosáuridos asiáticos.

facts.statement: In some of these analyses, Talarurus was the sister species of Nodocephalosaurus.
facts.quote: En algunos de estos , Talarurus era la especie hermana de Nodocephalosaurus.

facts.statement: It was previously supposed that, as one of the oldest known ankylosaurids, Talarurus possessed some basal characteristics shared with nodosaurids but later lost in advanced ankylosaurians, such as the presence of four toes on the feet.
facts.quote: Anteriormente se suponía que, como uno de los anquilosáuridos más antiguos conocidos, Talarurus poseía algunas características basales que se comparten con los nodosáuridos pero que luego se perdieron en los anquilosaurios más avanzados, como la presencia de cuatro dedos en los pies.

facts.statement: However, these supposed "primitive" traits were shown to be largely artifacts of the initial skeletal restoration.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, los supuestos rasgos "primitivos" demostraron ser en gran parte artefactos de la restauración esquelética inicial.

facts.statement: The fused, semi-rectangular maxilla was likely useful on flat surfaces.
facts.quote: probablemente útil en superficies planas.

facts.statement: The preserved left foot is very singular; while initially described as having four digits, it was proven to be an artifact of the initial mount, with three digits being more probable as seen in related ankylosaurids.
facts.quote: El pie izquierdo conservado es muy singular, se describió que tenía cuatro dígitos, sin embargo, se demostró que esta afirmación era un producto del montaje del esqueleto inicial y tres dígitos es más probable, como se ve en los anquilosáuridos relacionados.

facts.statement: A 2007 study examined the nearly complete and well-preserved skull specimen MPC-D 100/1354 to understand the neurocranium and dietary habits of Talarurus.
facts.quote: Los cráneos de especímenes de 2007 han aportado nuevos conocimientos sobre las capacidades neurocraneales y los hábitos dietéticos de Talarurus, específicamente el espécimen MPC-D 100/1354, que es un cráneo casi completo y bien conservado.

facts.statement: Researchers found that ankylosaurs, unlike nodosaurids, possessed well-developed eye stabilization and auditory senses based on endocranial region analysis.
facts.quote: Observaron que los anquilosáuridos tenían una estabilización de la mirada y sentidos auditivos bien desarrollados, a diferencia de los nodosáuridos, al examinar la región endocraneal de los especímenes seleccionados.

facts.statement: Maryańska first reported the flocculus in Talarurus, noting it is absent or reduced in nodosaurids compared to related ankylosaurs.
facts.quote: La presencia del flóculo fue reportada por primera vez en Talarurus por Maryańska y más tarde en otros anquilosáuridos relacionados, sin embargo, este lóbulo parece estar ausente o reducido en los nodosáuridos.

facts.statement: The elongated lagena indicates that ankylosaurs had a wide range of sound perception, particularly for low frequencies.
facts.quote: Esta característica anatómica indica que los anquilosáuridos tenían un amplio rango de percepción del sonido, especialmente para las bajas frecuencias.

facts.statement: The preserved mouth in specimen MPC-D 100/1354 is wide, nearly rectangular, and somewhat robust.
facts.quote: Además de estos hallazgos, la boca conservada en MPC-D 100/1354 es ancha, de forma casi rectangular y algo robusta.

facts.statement: Talarurus likely fed efficiently on low vegetation in flat terrain due to its wide mouth.
facts.quote: La amplia boca de Talarurus probablemente trabajó con eficiencia en vegetación baja en terreno plano.
